summary: Unresolved merged layout: it combines the 0x60-byte TextStyle record created by Text_Style_Create (0x001927E0), a Sound_SeqChannel/Sound_Track-like mixer/envelope block at +0x5C..+0x166 initialised by three constructors that live in the Sound module (0x0054EC70, 0x0054FD50, 0x00554910), and a Text_MsgWindow* at +0x175C used only by the 0x00666xxx record predicates. No single game object has this layout; field names are per-offset best evidence.
evidence: Generated from M1 names "Text_Style_*" because the three ctors were grouped with TextStyle; however the ctors initialise Sound_SeqChannel/Sound_Track offsets, and the 0x0066650C/0x00666628/0x00666570/0x00667108 predicates read self+0x175C (a Text_MsgWindow pointer) - see the field notes. Size 5984 is max_strong_field+4 (0x175C), not an allocation.

summary: One page of laid-out message text: owns the 6 equipment-glyph bytes, the typing cursor/deadline, the glyph arrays and the five packed layout coordinates, and is embedded in a Text_MsgWindow.
evidence: Ctor 0x00192450 stores vtable 0x007803AC, builds an intrusive-list node at +4/+8/+0xC, clears the 10 packed u16 coordinates at +0x1C8, then initialises the embedded layout state; Text_Page_Reset/BuildFromRecord/BuildAtOffset/SetContent/ExportLayout all operate on this page (R_039/R_059 docs). The +0x175C-style site is absent here: +0xC8 is a byte, validated in the ctor disassembly.

summary: Large UI message-block/row container (0x3D0C bytes, Actor_SubObject base): owns a circular row list, two intrusive list nodes, a source list and two sub-objects destroyed by its five dtor variants.

summary: NG-word (profanity filter) validator: wraps a 0x800-byte Svc_ContentObject service and four memory buffers, and masks/validates text through dictionary and regex paths.
evidence: Inherits Svc_ContentObject (base-ctor call in InitBuffers/OpenService); OpenService mounts a content service, ValidateAll/ValidateOne normalise text and call ApplyDictionary/MaskField/MatchWord; CloseService unmounts and clears the whole state.

fields.name: maybe_serviceReady
fields.evidence: Text_NgWord_CloseService (0x00515058) tests it before calling func_005099F8 and then clears it together with the mount/service state.

fields.name: isMounted
fields.evidence: Text_NgWord_OpenService (0x00514A20) sets it to 1 on success (strb r4,[r6,#0x19]); CloseService passes it to Fs_UnmountByName and clears it.

fields.name: maybe_skipDictionary
fields.evidence: Text_NgWord_ApplyDictionary and Text_NgWord_MaskField both branch around the pattern/regex replacement path when it is non-zero.

fields.name: currentChar
fields.evidence: ValidateAll/ValidateOne store the character being examined here; MatchWord/ApplyDictionary then write this byte over the masked positions of the caller text.

fields.name: maybe_scratchBufferA
fields.evidence: InitBuffers (0x005147EC) stores the caller memory base here; ValidateOne bails out when it is 0. One of two buffers based at the same block.

fields.name: maybe_scratchBufferB
fields.evidence: InitBuffers stores the same memory base here; MatchWord passes it to the regex initialiser (func_0051433C).

fields.name: maybe_patternBuffer
fields.evidence: InitBuffers sets it to base+0xB000; the next region base+0xF000 is stored at +0x28, so this is a 0x4000-byte work buffer (dictionary/pattern scratch).

fields.name: serviceObject
fields.evidence: InitBuffers sets it to base+0xF000 and OpenService passes it to maybe_Svc_ContentObject_CreateAndRegister(...,0x800,...) creating the 0x800-byte NG-word service object.

fields.name: normalizeBuffer
fields.evidence: InitBuffers sets it to base+0xF800; ApplyDictionary/ValidateOne use it+0x600 as the destination of Text_NormalizeFullwidth.

fields.name: unknown_u8_30
fields.evidence: CloseService sets it to 1 at the end; no reader in the corpus.

summary: Small (124-byte) renderer/animation binding holder: keeps up to three animator handles plus two releasable objects and one allocated block, all freed by its two destructor variants.
evidence: Both recovered functions are dtors; they call maybe_Ui_Animator_ReleaseBindings and then release objects through virtual slot 1, zeroing +0x34/+0x38, and free +0x3C via func_0010E66C/0x0056562C.

fields.name: maybe_animOwner

fields.name: maybe_bindingA

fields.name: maybe_bindingB
fields.evidence: Second handle passed to maybe_Ui_Animator_ReleaseBindings (Dtor2 uses +0x1C where Dtor uses +0xC).

fields.name: hasBindings
fields.evidence: Both dtors skip the animator-release block when it is 0.

fields.name: objectA
fields.evidence: Dtor calls virtual slot 1 (release) on the pointed object and zeroes the field.

fields.name: objectB
fields.evidence: Dtor2 calls virtual slot 1 on it and zeroes it; Dtor has the same pattern on +0x34.

fields.name: maybe_allocatedBlock
fields.evidence: Dtor frees it via func_0010E66C / func_0056562C depending on a branch, then clears the field.

fields.name: maybe_allocSizeOrOwner

fields.name: isReleased

fields.name: maybe_bindingC
fields.evidence: Dtor passes it together with +0xC/+0x18 to maybe_Ui_Animator_ReleaseBindings.

summary: Embedded page-layout builder inside the same 0x3D08-byte UI block as Text_Block: holds the line array (0x2C-byte entries), its count and the owner back-pointer, and rebuilds rows from the party list.
evidence: Text_LayoutPage_BuildLines (0x002FD45C) writes self+0x3768/+0x376C counts, walks self+0x3774..+0x3778 in 0x2C steps, stores self+0x12C at +0x3D04, and calls Text_LayoutLine_AutoSize per party member.

fields.name: maybe_lineState
fields.evidence: Text_LayoutPage_BuildLines addresses self+0x3574 as an int* (piVar9); no field of it is read in the recovered body.

fields.name: entryCount
fields.evidence: BuildLines stores the global list count (0x0072C0E0) into self+0x3000+0x768; later loops over that many entries and passes it to Ui_ListData_BuildEntries.

fields.name: rowCount
fields.evidence: BuildLines stores the party-member count here and uses it as the loop bound when building one row per member.

fields.name: lineList
fields.evidence: self+0x3000+0x770 is the embedded list/controller: BuildLines sets +0x594 from self+0x12C and walks its begin/end array (+4/+8, 0x2C-byte elements); BindSourceList passes it to a virtual slot.

fields.name: lineArrayBegin
fields.evidence: BuildLines walks from this pointer up to +0x3778 in 0x2C-byte steps (invalidates/reuses layout lines).

fields.name: lineArrayEnd
fields.evidence: Upper bound of the same 0x2C-byte line array; BuildLines clamps it to the found end.

fields.name: maybe_lineOwner
fields.evidence: BuildLines stores self+0x12C here (a back-pointer to the embedded line/row owner).

summary: 24-byte view/cursor over a string buffer: keeps the base, start, aligned start, end and a cursor position plus a flag word.
evidence: Text_StringView_Init (0x005508C4) stores the three pointer arguments, computes an aligned start (bic #0x1F) and clears the last two words; the helper at 0x00550900 walks from +0x14.

fields.name: text
fields.evidence: Text_StringView_Init stores its first pointer argument (arg1) here; the other fields are derived from the start/end pointers.

fields.name: start
fields.evidence: Init stores its second argument (arg2) here.

fields.name: maybe_alignedStart
fields.evidence: Init calls func_0011CFAC(arg2,arg3) and stores the result with the low 5 bits cleared (bic r1,r0,#0x1F); a 32-byte aligned start for the scan.

fields.name: end
fields.evidence: Init stores its third argument (arg3) here.

fields.name: maybe_position
fields.evidence: Init clears it; the same layout is used as a cursor (see the following Text_StringView helper that walks bits from +0x14).

fields.name: maybe_flags
fields.evidence: Init clears it; the helper at 0x00550900 uses +0x14 as a bitmap of visited entries.

summary: Per-window advance/queue state for one battle text window: a stage byte, window/sub-panel ids, a completion callback and its two arguments.
evidence: maybe_Text_WindowQueue_Advance (0x005BCB2C) dispatches on the stage byte at +4 (read but not in this field set), uses +0xC as window id, +0xD as sub-panel index, calls +0x10 as a completion callback and forwards +0x14/+0x18 as its arguments to Battle_TextWindow_EnsureSubPanel/func_0063339C.

fields.name: windowId
fields.evidence: maybe_Text_WindowQueue_Advance loads it and forwards it to func_0063339C on the text-window handle (ctx+0x31C) when advancing state 0.

fields.name: subPanelIndex
fields.evidence: Advance compares it with 1 and passes it to Battle_TextWindow_EnsureSubPanel(handle, self->f_D).

fields.name: onComplete
fields.evidence: Advance calls it through a register when the window finished (ip = *(u32*)(self+0x10); ip(arg0)).

fields.name: maybe_arg0
fields.evidence: Forwarded as the first of two words (with +0x18) to the completion call along with self and the owner; probably the completion arguments.

fields.name: maybe_arg1
fields.evidence: Second word forwarded with +0x14 to the completion path.

fields.name: maybe_status
fields.evidence: Read as a signed byte into a status local; no writer in the corpus.

fields.name: maybe_end

fields.name: maybe_cursor

fields.name: maybe_isReversed

fields.name: maybe_isValid

summary: Row-list scroller: clamps a base+extra offset to 0..127 and finds the last row whose position fits, using a list at +0x11C and a link node at +0xF8.

summary: 255-entry glyph cache of 0x18-byte key records: key words at +0x4/+0x8 and the array end at +0x17E8.

fields.name: maybe_key1
fields.evidence: Text_GlyphCache_FindOrInsert compares entries word-by-word: param_1[1] against the caller key (18h-byte entries, 0xFF of them).

fields.name: maybe_key2
fields.evidence: Third word of the same 0x18-byte cache key compared by FindOrInsert.

fields.name: maybe_cacheArrayEnd
fields.evidence: self+0x1400+0x3E8 is the end of the 255-entry (0xFF * 0x18 = 0x17E8) glyph cache array. It is the container end, not a key field; the 0x18-byte key record only really has +0..+0x17.
